lines.text: The rotten palisade comes down in an afternoon. The wall goes up over a week — grey stone out of the new quarry, wedge-cut, course on course. Where the road passes through, the masons raise a gateway: a ring of stones, and a keystone dropped home at the top.
It holds because every stone in that ring is being squeezed, and squeezing is the one thing stone can't lose at. Ask it to bend and it snaps. We stopped asking.
For the first time since the artefact, the town looks different from the hill: a stone ring where the wooden one stood. It is a small wall. It is a beginning.
